verdict.rationale: Logseq's own Export docs say whole graphs, pages, blocks or selections can be exported as standard Markdown, JSON, OPML, HTML, EDN and Roam JSON. Community users confirm working from local markdown files kept in a git repo. Caveats: one user reports the new DB version no longer stores notes as markdown files, and another calls Logseq's native Markdown/Org backends non-standard, though the export path to standard Markdown remains documented. Missing for 10: published schema documentation for the JSON/EDN export formats, hands-on verification that exports are complete and lossless, and confirmation that plain-file storage persists in the DB version.

support.subject: As a researcher, my notes are stored or exportable in open, documented formats (Markdown, JSON) so my archive outlives the vendor

citations.quote: The Logseq Export feature allows users to export their data in various formats, including text, HTML, OPML, PNG, EDN, JSON, and standard Markdown.
It supports exporting text selections, blocks, individual pages, or the entire graph with customizable options.
